apps.name: AtomiX
apps.description: v0.1.15: FUNDS — a lock that was refundable could become permanently unrefundable. Refund discovery was bounded to a 256-block chain scan, so a coin went invisible ~3h33m after it was locked while it was still refundable, and a lost node reply could wedge the refund retry for good. Both fixed; a refund is now driven from your own swap record, which has no such window. minimaSwap + usdtSwap combined into ONE app — pick your currency from the header pill and swap either native MINIMA ↔ ERC20, or bridged native-USDT (mxUSDT) ↔ ERC20 USDT. Trustless HTLC atomic swaps, no custodian. You publish and market-make in ONE currency at a time, and switching currency re-themes the whole app to that identity (Minima orange ↔ Tether green) and moves your market to that book — the legacy per-currency order books, so AtomiX interoperates with existing minimaSwap / usdtSwap peers. Background settlement is currency-agnostic: switching currency NEVER strands an in-flight swap in the other one. Carries the full feature set (depth-ladder market-making, best-price market-sweep taking, OTC tab, embedded ETH wallet, both directions, background watcher) plus the claim-path reliability hardening. v0.1.13: the Wallet tab's red Ethereum-RPC warning now clears itself. It was only ever set, never cleared, so ONE transient RPC or DNS blip pinned the message on screen until you restarted the app — even while balances underneath it kept updating normally. It now disappears on the next good read. v0.1.11: fund-safety — a harvested HTLC preimage is now verified to hash to the lock before it is trusted, so a forged on-chain reveal (the notify sink is anyone-can-write) can no longer poison the secret store and block your claim. v0.1.9: the Wallet tab gains Send — move ETH or USDT out to any address, with balance and gas checks, a Max button and a review step. v0.1.8: settlement hardening — a claim now verifies the received coin is the right token before completing, a mismatched counterparty lock can no longer hold up a valid claim, and the responder’s timing guard reads Ethereum chain time. v0.1.7: when several makers quote the same best price, a swap now fills the DEEPEST maker first — so a fillable amount uses one swap instead of splitting into extra legs (a strictly better price still always wins). v0.1.6: the live order book refreshes every ~90s and re-checks the maker at take time, so a market a maker has WITHDRAWN can no longer show as tradeable. v0.1.5: switching currency TOMBSTONES your live market on the old book and REMEMBERS each currency's market. v0.1.3: ladder defaults to a SINGLE level (multi-leg opt-in, up to 6) and the AtomiX atom icon. EXPERIMENTAL; test small.

apps.name: Minima ETH Wallet
apps.description: Standalone Ethereum/ERC20 wallet sharing minimaSwap's address — manage tokens, send/receive (QR), add any ERC20 by contract address, live gas preview, view activity on Etherscan. Same address via node-pair or one-time key import. 0.2.2 is a security and stability release, recommended for everyone. Fixes a crash-loop on launch: reinstalling restored the encrypted key store from backup, but the Keystore key that unlocks it is device-bound and is not restored, so the app died on every start — backup of that store is now disabled and an unreadable store is repaired instead of fatal. The confirm screen now shows the FULL recipient address instead of a shortened one, so address-poisoning (a lookalike address matching the first and last few characters) can no longer hide there, and recipients are checksum-verified. Node-derived keys are validated and the address is pinned: if your node ever derives a DIFFERENT address — a reset or restored-with-another-seed node — the wallet stops and tells you your funds are at the old address, instead of silently showing you an empty new wallet. Gas price and limit from the RPC are now bounded, so a bad endpoint cannot drain the balance as fees.

apps.name: Minima Wallet
apps.description: Self-custodial Minima wallet — signs locally, uses Minima Core only as a NON-admin relay (works with node admin OFF). PRE-VERIFICATION TEST BUILD: viewing balances + receiving is safe; do NOT send real funds until on-device verification confirms a transaction lands on-chain. Coins received are always recoverable from your seed. When importing a seed, enter how many signatures it has already used (over-estimate if unsure) — this protects against reusing a one-time key.

apps.name: FreezePeach
apps.description: Censorship-resistant, self-custodial chat on the MaxLite off-chain network. Your identity is your Minima seed — the same on any device — end-to-end sealed, no phone number, no account, no server that can read or block you. Premium two-theme design, scan/paste contacts, short IDs, group chats with media + admins, rich sealed photos/video, and a full photo editor: filters, adjust, crop, rotate, markup, plus a native retro-effects studio (filtr, ported to OpenGL ES): dithering & palettes, halftone, edge-detect, ASCII art, CRT, scanlines, RGB-split, bloom, grain. Now includes a full non-custodial in-app Minima wallet: local WOTS signing (seed never leaves the device), send to any address or straight to a contact from the chat with a payment bubble, token icons + names + web-validation checkmarks, and a live balance. 0.3.33 is a SECURITY release — upgrade strongly recommended: it fixes WOTS one-time-key re-use that could expose the key guarding your funds after a backup restore or a second-device setup, and domain-separates the wallet key from a Minima node's own key index 0, with a one-time upgrade screen and an attestation-gated sweep onto the new address.

apps.name: PandaPools

apps.name: PandaDEX
apps.description: v0.4.1: fixes the remaining trade-verification edge cases before public release — chain history now verifies the covenant-matched output for the exact spent order input, so batch cancels and same-wallet same-amount orders cannot cross-prove phantom fills; rows only claim CHAIN_VERIFIED when local node history proved the fill, otherwise payout evidence remains LOCAL_VERIFIED; exports keep PandaDEX local/node verification if explorer.minima.global or block.minima.global are unavailable, with both links included as optional corroboration; maker split:10 now blocks publishing until the split outputs confirm/sendable and cannot double-post while fetching the wallet address. On-chain DEX for MINIMA/mxUSDT blending PandaDEX V5 order-book liquidity with PandaPools AMM reserves. The ladder labels BOOK and POOL depth separately, marketable limits can fill atomically across both sources, and any unfilled balance rests as a limit order. Includes built-in market maker, a split:10 maker funding tool for preparing wallet UTXOs before publishing offers, confirmed personal trades, on-chain evidence/export for reconciliation, AtomiX mxUSDT bridge wording, and sendable/confirmed/locked/unconfirmed wallet balances. v0.4.0: a fill is now proven from the transaction that SPENT the order coin, not inferred from what is left unspent — so a fill whose proceeds were already spent onward is no longer lost, which is the normal case for your own maker rungs, and a cancel posted from another device on the same seed is seen correctly. Payout evidence is also adjudicated across a whole scan at once, so one cancelled rung's refund can no longer prove a payment for every other order of the same size (it produced three phantom trades on a live ladder). Anything still unproven is dropped. EXPERIMENTAL and it moves real funds — test small.

apps.name: KeyUses
apps.description: Audit your node's 64 keys for one-time-signature re-use. Minima signatures are stateful: each key must move to a fresh leaf every time it signs, and a seed re-sync that set keyuses too low makes the node re-use a leaf it already spent on-chain, which weakens that key. KeyUses compares what the chain proves each key has signed against your node's own counter, flags any key at risk or with confirmed re-use, and gives you the safe keyuses value for your next re-sync. Read-only: it never builds a transaction. Your 64 public keys are sent to the archive audit service to look up spend history — public keys cannot move funds, but they do reveal your addresses to that server.

apps.name: Brain Wallet
apps.description: Derive a Bitcoin, Litecoin or Ethereum wallet from a passphrase and salt — nothing is stored, nothing is transmitted, and the app asks for no permissions at all. Two derivation schemes. scrypt (N=2^18) reproduces legacy 1... addresses byte-for-byte with the Brain Wallet MiniDapp 1.0.14, so a wallet made there comes back identically here; this is the default. Argon2id (384MB, 25 iterations) produces native SegWit bc1q.../ltc1q... addresses and Ethereum, matching brainwallet.io v3.0.1 — verified against vectors generated from that site's own code, with a native ARM build of the reference Argon2 so it takes ~8 seconds instead of ~75. Address and private key shown as text and QR. ⚠️ A brain wallet has NO checksum and NO recovery: one wrong character silently derives a different, perfectly valid wallet that is not yours. Verify recovery on a second device before funding, and store the passphrase and salt as exact byte-for-byte artifacts.

apps.name: Entropy
apps.description: Provably fair BIP39 seed phrase generator — roll animated dice for maximum entropy. Each face = SHA3(node random ++ device SecureRandom) rejection-sampled to exact uniformity; maths locked bit-for-bit to iancoleman/bip39 by fixed vectors. Physical-dice mode, per-roll audit log, Last Word checksum calculator with 4-char autocomplete. Zero permissions, FLAG_SECURE, nothing stored or transmitted — closing the app destroys the phrase.
